html:
Baji Rao I was peshwa, chief minister, of the Maratha king from 1720 to 1740. In twenty years he turned a regional kingdom into the Maratha Confederacy that reached across India. He is said never to have lost a battle.

He took office at nineteen, after his father. He told the king that the Mughal Empire was a withered tree: strike the trunk and the branches will fall. His weapon was cavalry that moved without baggage, lived off the land and covered sixty kilometres a day.

  • 1728: at Palkhed he trapped the Nizam of Hyderabad without water and forced him to terms.
  • 1729: he rode to the aid of the old king of Bundelkhand and was given a third of that kingdom.
  • 1737: he slipped past a Mughal army, appeared outside Delhi, and left again within days. Its weakness was now plain; two years later came Nader Shah.
  • 1738: he beat the Nizam again near Bhopal and won Malwa.

He gave conquered lands to his commanders, the Holkars, Scindias and Gaekwads, who became princes in their own right. He made Pune the Maratha capital and built the Shaniwar Wada palace there. His love for Mastani, a Muslim, caused a scandal among the Brahmins of Pune. He died of fever on campaign, aged thirty-nine.
